teaser.text: JD.com is a Chinese retailer that also runs a marketplace and sells shopping infrastructure to other businesses. A dollar enters through goods, commissions, advertising, memberships and business services, then leaves through products, people, buildings, delivery and the costs of winning the next order.

blocks.heading: Where could JD.com’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: JD.com’s weighted path is HK$196.12 in October 2027 (+89%) and HK$285.37 in October 2029 (+180%), but it hinges on earnings recovery, smaller New Businesses losses and continued capital returns. Management expects group revenue to return to positive growth in the second half of 2026 and JD Retail to return to growth in Q3, alongside stronger group profit growth and substantially smaller food-delivery losses.

The forecast puts JD.com at HKD196.12 in October 2027, HKD239.81 in October 2028 and HKD285.37 in October 2029, including dividends. These prices imply returns of 89%, 133% and 180% from HKD106.20. By 2029, however, the bear case reaches HKD74.44 while the bull case reaches HKD670.73, so the probability-weighted figure conceals substantial execution risk.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for JD.com—and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The central case is a recovery in earnings, continued buybacks and a measured valuation. The bear case reflects weak demand and continuing losses in New Businesses; the bull case requires stronger marketplace growth, better logistics productivity and a higher multiple.

The bull case requires third-party marketplace activity to outgrow first-party sales, logistics efficiency to improve and food-delivery subsidies to fall. Stronger cash generation then supports buybacks and a 22x multiple. Prices reach HKD357.09 first and HKD670.73 last, with a 20% probability. The upside is credible because JD has more than one million marketplace merchants and faster 3P than 1P GMV growth, but sustained execution is unproven.

blocks.heading: How much cash does JD.com really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow subtracts spending on warehouses, equipment and software from operating cash. Treating stock compensation as an economic cost produces a stricter measure because employees receive a claim that otherwise belongs to existing owners. JD’s own free-cash-flow measure is higher because it adjusts consumer-financing receivables and uses capital spending net of related sales proceeds. That definition may be reasonable, but it is not interchangeable with the simpler measure.

blocks.heading: How much does JD.com pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend remains CNY3.50 per share throughout. The bear case holds at CNY3.50 initially, then falls to CNY2.10 by 2029; the bull case rises to CNY4.90. Stability is supported by the unchanged US$0.50 dividend for 2024 and 2025, but 2025 free cash flow was only CNY1,200m against CNY10,379m of dividends, so the board’s flexibility is not unlimited.

blocks.heading: Does JD.com cover its dividend with free cash flow?

paragraphs.text: The position changed in 2025. Free cash flow fell sharply, while dividends and buybacks remained large. Shareholders received more than the business generated internally that year. JD could fund the gap from its wider financial resources, but doing so reduced the cushion available for expansion, acquisitions and new ventures.

blocks.heading: What could change the JD.com dividend?

paragraphs.text: The view moves toward the bull case if third-party GMV continues to outgrow first-party activity, delivery efficiency improves during 2027–2028 and free cash flow strengthens. Sustained buybacks and a higher dividend would reinforce that evidence, while a re-rating in 2028 would confirm that investors regard the earnings recovery as durable.

earnings.opening: JD.com’s next results are expected on November 12, 2026. Watch whether returning customers and marketplace activity grow profitably after incentives fade.
earnings.closing: The full JD.com memo also answers how its business works, who its rivals are, how management is paid and controlled, and which risks matter.

blocks.heading: What has JD.com guided for the second half of 2026?

paragraphs.text: JD’s Q2 2026 revenue fell 2.9%. Finance chief Ian Su Shan said group revenue should return to positive growth in the second half of 2026, while JD Retail, its core shopping business, should return to growth in Q3.

Management also expects stronger group profit growth and substantially smaller food-delivery losses in the second half. But a subsidized delivery order creates value only if the customer later shops often enough, and profitably enough, to cover the cost of attracting and serving them.

blocks.heading: What is JD.com’s revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: JD.com is a Chinese commerce and delivery company whose accounts combine retail, logistics and newer bets. Read together, they show a business that grew faster in 2025 but converted less of that activity into operating profit and cash, while its latest quarter offers a promising but incomplete repair.

Revenue declined from the prior-year quarter, while gross margin and operating income improved. JD therefore earned more from a smaller revenue base. That is evidence of better economics, not proof that demand had returned.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in JD.com’s next results?

paragraphs.text: Q3 results are expected on November 12, 2026. Watch purchasing users, purchase frequency, third-party purchasing users and third-party orders using consistent definitions. A third-party seller is an independent merchant using JD’s marketplace rather than selling inventory owned by JD. More marketplace orders can bring commissions, advertising and logistics revenue without requiring JD to own every product.
